title: Shared Google Workspace identity
summary: One Google Workspace Account in Parameter Store can authorize Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive. Its googleaccount record owns the private access/refresh tokens, verified Google.
html:
Shared Google Workspace identity

One Google Workspace Account in Parameter Store can authorize Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive. Its google_account record owns the private access/refresh tokens, verified Google subject and email, expiry and granted scopes. There is no second credential database. Existing gmail_oauth_app and gmail_account records remain supported; opening or using them never migrates them.

Configure and connect

Enable Authentication in Capability Policy. In Parameter Store → New, choose Google Workspace OAuth App, supply your own registered Google client ID, and save the parameter as workspace_app. No Workspace scopes are selected by default. Use the Value JSON editor to set requested_features, or name features when connecting. Leave requested_scopes empty to derive them; if populated, it must exactly match the selected feature scopes. This field cannot authorize arbitrary scope expansion.

{
  "profile_type": "google_oauth_app",
  "profile_version": 1,
  "service": "google_workspace",
  "client_type": "desktop",
  "client_id": "YOUR_REGISTERED_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "",
  "authorization_uri": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth",
  "token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",
  "redirect_uri": "",
  "requested_features": ["calendar_read"],
  "requested_scopes": []
}

Desktop clients generate a temporary 127.0.0.1 loopback listener on the controller. Do not save its random port. Supply Google's desktop client secret if your registered client requires it. Desktop clients cannot keep that value confidential from their owner. For a remote controller, use a registered web client, its client secret, and the exact HTTPS callback https://YOUR_CONTROLLER/api/agent/google/oauth/callback. HTTP callbacks are allowed only for literal loopback development addresses.

Ask to connect with auth.google_connect:

{"auth_app_ref":"workspace_app","account_key":"workspace","features":["calendar_read"]}

The result contains an authorization link and the requested scope classifications. Open it and complete Google consent within ten minutes. auth.google_accounts lists safe connected identities; auth.google_status inspects a chosen account and optional required features. Connection grants access only to features actually granted by Google. A successful authorization may still lack a feature if consent was partial.

Add Drive file access later with the same key:

{"auth_app_ref":"workspace_app","account_key":"workspace","features":["drive_file"]}

Web clients use Google's incremental grant option. Google does not support incremental authorization for installed applications, so desktop upgrades request renewed consent for the prior grants plus the selected new features. Both update the existing record. The application never assumes an unreturned permission was granted. New authorization requires a returned scope list; refresh responses may omit it and retain the prior grant.

The first connection explicitly requests consent and offline access so a refresh token can be issued. Web upgrades retain an existing refresh token when Google omits a new one; if none exists, consent is requested again. Desktop upgrades explicitly request consent. No-key creation derives a stable key from the verified subject. If accounts already exist for the app, select the intended key before reconnecting. Creating another profile for that identity requires an explicitly different key.

Feature permissions

Every suffix below is prefixed with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/. All new connections also request openid email to verify the stable Google identity. They do not request the unrelated OIDC profile scope.

Feature Requested scope suffix Classification
gmail_read gmail.readonly Restricted
gmail_modify gmail.modify Restricted
gmail_send gmail.send Sensitive
calendar_list calendar.calendarlist.readonly Check Google Cloud Console
calendar_read calendar.events.readonly Sensitive
calendar_freebusy calendar.freebusy Check Google Cloud Console
calendar_write calendar.events Sensitive
drive_file drive.file Non-sensitive
drive_metadata_read drive.metadata.readonly Restricted
drive_read_all drive.readonly Restricted
drive_write_all drive Restricted
gmail_drafts gmail.compose Restricted
gmail_drafts_read gmail.readonly Restricted
gmail_labels / gmail_labels_read gmail.labels Non-sensitive
gmail_settings gmail.settings.basic Restricted
gmail_settings_read gmail.readonly Restricted

drive_file covers files created by or specifically shared with the application; it is not a Drive-wide search grant. calendar_read covers events; listing calendar subscriptions additionally requires calendar_list. calendar_freebusy covers the user's availability, not event details. calendar_write edits events, not calendar ACLs or calendar management. Requesting gmail_modify inherently permits sends and reads under Google's scope definition; requesting gmail_read never adds modification.

The scope engine recognizes documented broader grants for availability without requesting them automatically. For example, an existing gmail.modify grant satisfies Gmail reads and sends, and drive satisfies file/read/metadata operations. A read-only Drive grant never satisfies file writes. Calendar event editing alone does not satisfy the separate free/busy endpoint. Gmail draft-send requires gmail.compose or gmail.modify; gmail.send alone supports direct message sending.

Sensitive scopes can require Google application verification. Restricted scopes can also require a security assessment. Google’s Calendar scope reference does not publish per-scope sensitivity classifications for calendar listing/free-busy; results explicitly say console-defined for those two scopes. Review their current sensitivity indicators in your Google Cloud project's Data Access screen before publishing.

Scope definitions and OAuth behavior were checked against the official OAuth overview, desktop OAuth guidance, Calendar scopes, Drive scopes, Gmail scopes, and sensitive-scope guidance on September 30–October 1, 2026. Google's scope directory identifies Cloud Console as the authority for sensitivity indicators.

Identity, privacy and Gmail reuse

Google's signed ID token establishes the subject (sub) and verified email. Signature, issuer, audience, timestamps, nonce and authorized party are checked. A changed email with the same subject is allowed; a changed subject cannot replace an existing key. Access tokens, refresh tokens, client secrets, authorization codes, ID tokens and PKCE verifiers are never tool results or ordinary context. ID tokens and handshakes are not saved. Only account token bundles and app secrets persist in Parameter Store. These privacy boundaries apply even when optional redaction switches are off.

Enable Gmail and use @workspace with the existing gmail.* tools. Search requires Gmail read access, message/label-state mutation requires modification, and direct sending requires send access. Compose drafts, label administration and filters have their own narrow requirements. Reply/forward also require read access to the original message. Missing permission produces google.scope_upgrade_required with the exact account and missing features. Reconnect that account; the runtime never silently substitutes another. A send-only account cannot reconcile an uncertain send through a Sent search; the existing unknown-effect protection still prevents automatic resending.

Resolution uses an explicit key, then an accepted eligible account binding, then a single configured eligible account. Multiple eligible accounts require selection. An explicitly selected account with missing access fails on that account, even if another is available. Accepted references pin identity while refresh resolves current Parameter Store authority. Renaming/deleting/replacing the account invalidates its old reference.

Refresh updates the same token bundle through Parameter Store revision checks. Concurrent requests in one controller process share a bounded lock across service and store instances. Cross-process writes are fenced against account and app revisions; they do not provide a distributed refresh lease. Run one controller process for a given Parameter Store. A revoked refresh grant returns google.reauthorization_required and records that status.

Calendar and Drive domain adapters request a feature from the shared provider and use the same account; they need no credential file, account database, Gmail dependency, or helper model. Google SMTP's generic Auth profiles remain a separate existing contract; this feature does not silently convert them.

For a trusted domain adapter, resolve the accepted binding before obtaining a token:

from agent_runtime.auth.google import provider_for

provider = provider_for(parameter_store)
selected = provider.profiles.account(account_ref, context, required_features=["calendar_read"])
private_record = provider.authorized_account(
    selected.normalized_key, required_features=["calendar_read"]
)
# Pass private_record.value_json["access_token"] only to the trusted provider client.
# Return provider.profiles.summary(private_record) when exposing account metadata.

This private execution boundary must never serialize the record into tool results, Working Context, Memory or logs. Repeat the feature check when obtaining refreshed authority because Google can return a reduced grant.
